_comment: What a vault is made of, in the one place both processes read it from.
electron/main.js requires this; src/vault-paths.js imports it and hands
the renderer the matchers built from it. A fact stated here once cannot
have the two sides disagreeing about it — which is what a note the tree
shows and the editor will not open comes down to.
languageFlagPattern is a source string rather than a literal because a
regular expression is not a JSON type; both readers build it with the `u`
flag, which is what makes the \u{...} escapes mean codepoints.
_code_comment: Source files: text the vault opens and edits, but does not read as prose.
This list only says *that* a file is source. Which language it is written
in is not restated here — src/languages.js already carries every one of
these spellings as an alias of a language id, and src/highlight.js turns
that id into a parser. An extension added here without a matching alias
there opens as plain text rather than breaking, which is the right way
round for a list this long.
Extensions only, and no dotfiles: the vault walk hides anything beginning
with a dot, so `.gitignore` could not appear in the tree even if it were
_data_comment: Separated text — a table on disk rather than a document. Unlike the source
list above these do not open in the editor at all: they get a grid, the
way a PDF gets a page viewer. See src/csv.js. The delimiter each one is
read with is stated here so the reader never has to guess it.
